diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, for any \(\delta > 0\), any parameters \((\theta^i)_{i=1}^{9},(\bar{\theta}^i)_{i=1}^{d}, (\tilde{\theta}^i)_{i=1}^{d}\), and sufficiently large \(\mathcal{W}, \mathcal{L} \in \mathbb{N}\) such that \(\log_2(\mathcal{W}) \le \mathcal{L}\), there exist neural networks \(u_{\theta}\) and \(f_{\bar{\theta}}\)

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the weighted residual at the mollified exact solution solely by mollification errors, which is valid only if the weighted residual vanishes at the exact solution. With the per-term weights of eq:barRQ1, the PDE gives R_bar(u,f) = (phi^1-phi^3) dt u + sum_i (phi^3-phi^{bar i}) d_ii u + (phi^2-phi^3) v(u), which is nonzero for non-identical weights; e.g. constant weights phi^1=2 with all other weights 1 give ||R_bar_Q^1(u,f)||_Q = ||dt u||_{L^2(Q_T)}/sqrt(|Q_T|), which does not tend to 0 as eps->0, contradicting the claimed bound P(1+L_v) delta/sqrt(|Q_T|). The same omission occurs in the boundary estimate: at the exact solution the weighted boundary residual contains (phi^6(0)-phi^7(0)) u_0 and (phi^8(T)-phi^9(T)) z_0, so the trace estimate fails already at u_theta = u. Since the theorems quantify over arbitrary weight parameters, the proofs are invalid; the statements are also untenable for general weights (e.g. the degenerate choice phi^1(t,x)=t makes the weighted equation overdetermined by the two time boundary conditions, so the loss infimum is bounded away from zero for generic data), and no argument in the source establishes solvability of the weighted problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either (i) restrict the weight networks to a single common weight (reducing the method to the standard PINN and withdrawing the per-term weighting), or (ii) assume well-posedness of the weighted boundary value problem with uniform approximation rates and add the weight-mismatch terms to the residual estimates. Either way the advertised arbitrary-weights guarantee is abandoned.
issues.overall_effect: The approximation guarantees of thm:errorHeat, thm:errorWave, thm:errorHeatb and thm:errorWaveb are unreliable: the advertised smallness of the weighted loss for arbitrary fixed weights does not hold, and the prose conclusion that the total WeightedPINN loss can be made arbitrarily small by an appropriate choice of width and depth is unsupported.
issues.title: Weighted residual estimates drop weight-mismatch terms; the approximation theorems fail for arbitrary weights
issues.why_classification: The central quantifier (small weighted loss for ANY fixed weight parameters) is false as stated and unprovable by the given argument; every supported repair either trivializes the result (weights identically 1) or adds a nontrivial solvability hypothesis, a major loss of the advertised content for all four approximation theorems.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the weight networks \(\phi_{\theta^{i}},\phi_{\bar\theta^{i}},\phi_{\tilde\theta^{i}}\) belong to a function class that contains the constant function \(1\)

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis takes the maximum of the min-max objective over a weight class that is not required to be bounded (only the constant function 1 must belong to it). Sending one weight network to a large constant c gives, from the initial-condition term and its penalty, a leading behavior c^2 (lambda ||u_theta(0)||^2_{L^2(Omega)}/|Gamma| - rho |Omega|), and similarly c^2 (||dt u_theta||^2_{L^2(Q_T)}/|Q_T| - rho |Q_T|) from the equation residual; hence the maximum is +infinity unless ||u_theta(0)||^2 <= rho |Omega||Gamma|/lambda and analogous smallness holds. Since a small loss forces ||u_theta(0)|| approximately ||u_0||, the supposition is unsatisfiable for large data, and the implication is vacuous as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a uniform bound on the weight networks (e.g. |phi| <= M, as in the numerics where weights are restricted to [0.2,5]); this one-line hypothesis addition makes the inner maximum finite and preserves the method, conclusion, and advertised scope.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, thm:error_estHeat and thm:error_estWave are vacuous for large data (their hypothesis cannot be satisfied by any networks), so they establish nothing until a uniform bound on the weight class is added; the prose claim that small weighted loss implies approximation is consequently unsupported.
issues.title: The min-max hypothesis of the a-posteriori theorems is vacuous for unbounded weight classes
issues.why_classification: The defect is a missing standard local condition (a uniform weight bound); the short repair preserves every substantive claim and guarantee, so minor.

issues.failure_explanation: The comparison state u_bar is defined as the solution of the heat equation with terminal condition u_bar(T)=z_0 and control f_bar_theta, a backward parabolic problem that is ill-posed and for which the cited Cazenave reference (forward theory) gives no existence. The energy inequality is then integrated from t to T, bounding the earlier-time energy by the terminal data and future residuals: the reverse of the parabolic direction, and false in general (for V=0 and R=0, u_hat(t)=e^{(t-T)Delta}u_hat(T), and high eigenmodes give ||u_hat(0)|| = e^{lambda_n T} ||u_hat(T)||). The energy identity also drops the boundary term +int_{dOmega} u_theta d_nu u_bar (the Neumann trace of u_bar is not controlled by the loss), and the source is mis-defined as R = dt u_theta - Delta u_theta + V u_theta - f_bar_theta 1_omega instead of the plain residual with v(u_theta), so ||R|| is not controlled by the loss.

failure_location.quote: Applying Gr\"onwall's inequality to \eqref{eq:energy} gives, for any $t\in[0,T]$, $\|\hat u(t)\\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2} \le e^{C_{0}(T-t)}\Bigl( \|\hat u(T)\\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2} +C_{0}\!\int_{t}^{T}\!\bigl(\|R(s)\\|_{L^{2}(\Omega)}^{2} +\|u_{\theta}(s)\\|_{H^{1}(\partial\Omega)}^{2}\bigr)\, ds -\int_{t}^{T}\|\hat{u}\|^2_{H^1(\Omega)}ds\Bigr)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-anchor the argument at t=0: define u_bar by the forward problem with control f_bar_theta and initial data u_bar(0)=u_theta(0), run the energy estimate forward in time, treat the nonzero boundary trace by a lifting argument, use the correct residual R = dt u_theta - Delta u_theta + v(u_theta) - f_bar_theta 1_omega, and justify the control bound via uniqueness of the control (backward uniqueness) together with the minimal-control cost estimate. The stated conclusion is expected to survive this contained rework.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusion of thm:error_estHeat (small weighted loss implies max-time L^2 and L^2(0,T;H^1) approximation of the state and L^2(q_T) approximation of the control) is unproven; the proof's central energy estimate is invalid.
issues.title: The a-posteriori heat estimate relies on an ill-posed backward heat problem and a backward Grönwall inequality
issues.why_classification: The proof is invalid at its core (backward-in-time parabolic estimate), but a contained reworking (forward anchoring plus lifting) avoids new global proof architecture and preserves the advertised conclusion, so moderate.

issues.failure_explanation: Three defects: (i) the energy identity drops the boundary term -int_{dOmega} dt u_theta d_nu u_bar: since u_hat = u_theta on Sigma_T and u_bar = 0 there, d_nu u_hat = d_nu u_theta - d_nu u_bar, and the Neumann trace of u_bar is not controlled by the loss; (ii) the claimed backward Grönwall bound E(t) <= e^{C_0(T-t)}(E(T)+...) does not follow from the one-sided inequality d_t E <= C_0 E + g (the one-sided inequality permits arbitrarily fast decay, e.g. E' = -100 E, which violates the claimed bound); a valid estimate requires the two-sided bound |d_t E| <= C_0 E + g, available from the identity, and a backward Grönwall lemma applied to the integral of E; (iii) the source is mis-defined as R = d_tt u_theta - Delta u_theta + V u_theta - f_bar_theta 1_omega instead of the plain residual with v(u_theta), so ||R|| is not controlled by the loss. Unlike the heat case the terminal-anchored wave energy is well-posed, and each defect admits a contained repair, so the conclusion is expected to survive.

The wave experiments in Situations 4 and 8 use Omega = (-1,1)^10 with d = 10, whose diameter is 2 sqrt(10) about 6.32 > T = 3, so those experiments lie outside the theorem's regime; in addition no a-posteriori result is stated for the bilinear control problems, which account for half of the experiments (Situations 5-8). The narrative that the experiments support the theoretical findings is therefore overstated for those cases.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For simplicity, we use the $L^2$-norm formulation of the loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The implemented training losses are not the WeightedPINN residuals analyzed in the theory: the numerics use a single weight phi_{theta^2} on the full discrete Laplacian (eq:lossheat, and analogously eq:losswave) instead of independent weights phi_{bar theta^i} on each second derivative (eq:barRQ1, eq:barRQ2); the implemented boundary loss contains only the Dirichlet term sum (phi_{theta^5} u_theta)^2 and omits the derivative terms ||phi^5 dt u_theta|| and sum ||phi^{tilde i} d_{x_i} u_theta|| of the analyzed method; and the wave initial conditions are penalized in L^2 rather than the analyzed H^1 x L^2 penalties. Hence the convergence and stability theorems (thm:errorHeat, thm:errorWave, thm:error_estHeat, thm:error_estWave) do not apply to the procedure actually trained, and the claim that the experiments support the theoretical findings is not accurate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Align the two formulations: either implement the per-direction weighted residuals of eq:barRQ1/eq:barRG1 (and the H^1 boundary penalties) in the experiments, or re-run the analysis for the simpler implemented loss; both are contained but nontrivial.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical guarantees and the reported experiments concern two different procedures; the numerical validation does not cover the analyzed WeightedPINN method.
issues.title: The training losses actually implemented differ from the WeightedPINN residuals covered by the theory
issues.why_classification: The method actually trained differs from the method analyzed, so the theoretical guarantees do not cover the reported experiments; reconciling them requires a nontrivial re-implementation or re-analysis, but no central result is abandoned, so moderate.
